ch44.title: A Night on Olivet
ch44.b002: As they passed out of the temple that Tuesday afternoon, Matthew pointed to the great buildings. “⟦Q 176:0.1⟧Master, observe what manner of buildings these are. See the massive stones and the beautiful adornment; can it be that these buildings are to be destroyed?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered as they went on toward Olivet: “⟦Q 176:0.1⟧You see these stones and this massive temple; verily, verily, I say to you: In the days soon to come there shall not be left one stone upon another. They shall all be thrown down.⟦/Q⟧” The apostles walked behind him in wonder. They could imagine no event short of the end of the world that would bring down the temple.
ch44.b003: To avoid the crowds streaming along the Kidron valley, they climbed a short way up the western slope of the mount. Looking back, they saw the temple glorified by the rays of the setting sun. As they lingered, the lights of the city appeared one by one and the temple shone in the dusk, and there, under the mellow light of the full moon, Jesus and the twelve sat down. Presently Nathaniel asked, “⟦Q 176:0.2⟧Tell us, Master, how shall we know when these events are about to come to pass?⟦/Q⟧”
ch44.b004: Jesus answered calmly. After he left them, many would come as deliverers and lead many astray; they must not be deceived. They should not be troubled by wars and rumors of wars, by famines or earthquakes. They would be thrown out of the synagogue and put in prison, and some of them would be killed. But when they stood before judges, they need not be anxious about what to say, for the spirit would teach them in that very hour. “⟦Q 176:1.1⟧For a time you may be hated by all men for my sake, but even in these persecutions I will not forsake you; my spirit will not desert you. Be patient!⟦/Q⟧” And when they saw Jerusalem encompassed by the Roman armies, they must flee to the mountains without stopping to save anything. The apostles sat in silence in the moonlight a long time while these words sank in. Years later, at the first appearance of the Roman troops, practically the entire body of believers fled from Jerusalem in obedience to this warning and found safe shelter in Pella.
ch44.b006: Yet the apostles could think of the fall of the city only as part of the end of the world, bound up with the coming of a New Jerusalem and of new heavens and a new earth. So Peter asked how they would know when he would return to bring all this about. Jesus was thoughtful for some time. Then he said: “⟦Q 176:1.7⟧You ever err since you always try to attach the new teaching to the old; you are determined to misunderstand all my teaching; you insist on interpreting the gospel in accordance with your established beliefs. Nevertheless, I will try to enlighten you.⟦/Q⟧”
ch44.b007: His kingdom, he reminded them, was not of this world. He would soon leave them, but his spirit would be poured out upon all flesh, and in the meantime the Spirit of Truth would comfort and guide them. “⟦Q 176:2.3⟧Very soon must I leave you and take up the work the Father has intrusted to my hands, but be of good courage, for I will sometime return.⟦/Q⟧” He went on: “⟦Q 176:2.4⟧You behold me now in weakness and in the flesh, but when I return, it shall be with power and in the spirit. The eye of flesh beholds the Son of Man in the flesh, but only the eye of the spirit will behold the Son of Man glorified by the Father.⟦/Q⟧” The time of his return was known only in the councils of Paradise; not even the angels of heaven knew it. Still, they should learn to discern the signs of the times, as men know that summer is near when the fig tree puts forth tender branches. And then he turned their thoughts homeward: what the whole world must face at the end of an age, each of them must face personally when he came to the end of his natural life and passed through the portal of death.
ch44.b008: Of all the discourses the Master ever gave his apostles, none became so confused in their minds as this one, and so the later written accounts of that evening agree very little. No part of the gospel record ever suffered such misconstruction. But the Apostle John never became thus confused.
ch44.b010: It was late when the thirteen reached the new camp, speechless and under great emotional strain. Judas had finally confirmed his decision to abandon his associates. David Zebedee, John Mark, and a number of the leading disciples welcomed them, but no one wanted to sleep. As some twenty of them gathered about the campfire, Thomas asked: “⟦Q 176:3.1⟧Since you are to return to finish the work of the kingdom, what should be our attitude while you are away on the Father’s business?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus looked them over by the firelight. The downfall of nations, the end of an age, even the end of the world—what had these to do with one who believed the gospel? “⟦Q 176:3.2⟧What does it matter to you who believe this gospel of the kingdom if nations overturn, the age ends, or all things visible crash, since you know that your life is the gift of the Son, and that it is eternally secure in the Father?⟦/Q⟧” But this survival faith, he warned, was a living faith, and it must increasingly bear the fruits of the spirit.
ch44.b011: Then he told them the parable of the talents. A great man going on a long journey gave one servant five talents, another two, and another one. The first two traded and doubled what they had received, and to each the master said, “⟦Q 176:3.4⟧Well done, good and faithful servant, you have been faithful over a few things; I will now set you as steward over many.⟦/Q⟧” The third, afraid of his lord, hid his talent in the earth, and even that was taken from him. “⟦Q 176:3.5⟧You cannot stand still in the affairs of the eternal kingdom. … And remember that, inasmuch as you minister to one of the least of my brethren, you have done this service to me.⟦/Q⟧” As they went at last to their rest, he said: “⟦Q 176:3.10⟧Freely have you received; therefore freely should you give of the truth of heaven, and in the giving will this truth multiply and show forth the increasing light of saving grace, even as you minister it.⟦/Q⟧”
ch44.b013: When the work of teaching did not press them, Jesus and the apostles rested on Wednesdays. That morning an ominous silence hung over the camp, and breakfast was late and quiet. At last Jesus told them to rest that day, to think over all that had happened and meditate on what was ahead. He told Andrew that he would be absent all day and that no one was to go within the gates of Jerusalem.
ch44.b014: David Zebedee wanted to send three well-armed Galileans with him. Jesus declined. “⟦Q 177:0.3⟧No man will lay hands on me until that hour when I am ready to lay down my life in conformity to my Father’s will. These men may not accompany me. I desire to go alone, that I may commune with the Father.⟦/Q⟧” As he started off, young John Mark came forward with a small basket of food and water. The Master smiled and reached down to take it, but the lad held on. If he went along to carry the lunch, he said, the Master would be freer to worship, and he would surely be silent; he would ask no questions and would stay by the basket while Jesus went apart to pray. There they stood, both of them holding the basket. Presently the Master let go. “⟦Q 177:1.2⟧Since with all your heart you crave to go with me, it shall not be denied you. We will go off by ourselves and have a good visit. … Follow on with me.⟦/Q⟧”
ch44.b015: That day has become known on high as “⟦Q 177:1.3⟧the day which a young man spent with God in the hills.⟦/Q⟧” Jesus spent his last day of quiet on earth visiting with this truth-hungry youth and talking with his Paradise Father. He compared their childhoods and talked for more than an hour about home life, telling John that he would prove loyal because he had grown up in a home where love prevailed and wisdom reigned. He assured him that he would live to become a mighty messenger of the kingdom. As they turned back toward the camp, he said, “⟦Q 177:1.5⟧Well, John, we have had a good visit, a real day of rest, but see to it that you tell no man the things which I told you.⟦/Q⟧” John Mark never did. Through the few hours that remained, he never let the Master out of his sight for long; he slept only when Jesus slept.
ch44.b017: The apostles spent most of the day walking about Olivet and visiting with the disciples encamped with them, but by early afternoon they were anxious and inexpressibly lonely. Not one of them, save Judas, did not wish himself in John Mark’s place. Nathaniel said it to half a dozen of them: “⟦Q 177:3.2⟧What is wrong with most of us is that we are only halfhearted. We fail to love the Master as he loves us. If we had all wanted to go with him as much as John Mark did, he would surely have taken us all.⟦/Q⟧”
ch44.b018: About four o’clock runners reached David Zebedee. Several days earlier David had become convinced that the rulers would kill Jesus, and that the Master would neither use his divine power to save himself nor let his followers defend him. He had sent word to his mother in Bethsaida, urging her to come at once and to bring Mary the mother of Jesus and all his family. Now the runners reported that they were on the way. Since he had done this on his own initiative, David told no one.
ch44.b020: Shortly after Jesus and John Mark left the camp, Judas disappeared. In spite of the Master’s request, he hurried into Jerusalem to the home of Caiaphas the high priest, where an informal meeting of the Sanhedrin had been called to frame the charges against Jesus. The day before, Judas had told certain Sadducean friends that Jesus was a well-meaning dreamer, not the deliverer of Israel, and that he wished to withdraw gracefully. They had flattered him with promises of high honors from the Sanhedrin.
ch44.b021: He could not endure the humiliating thought of being identified with a movement of defeat. Now, as never before, he resented that Jesus had never given him a position of greater honor, and on the way to the high priest’s house he was bent on getting even with Peter, James, and John more than on any thought of betraying Jesus. A terrible conspiracy of confusion, pride, desperation, and determination had seized him. It was not for money that Judas went to Caiaphas.
ch44.b022: His cousin presented him to the rulers as one who had discovered his mistake and who could arrange for Jesus to be taken quietly, without stirring up the multitude. Then Judas stepped forward. “⟦Q 177:4.7⟧All that my cousin has promised, I will do, but what are you willing to give me for this service?⟦/Q⟧” He did not seem to discern the disdain and even disgust that crossed the face of Caiaphas. “⟦Q 177:4.8⟧Judas, you go to the captain of the guard and arrange with that officer to bring your Master to us either tonight or tomorrow night, and when he has been delivered by you into our hands, you shall receive your reward for this service.⟦/Q⟧” Judas and the captain of the temple guards agreed to make the arrest on Thursday evening, after the city and all the pilgrims had retired for the night.
ch44.b023: Jesus loved and trusted Judas just as he loved and trusted the others, but Judas never returned that love wholeheartedly. Deep in his heart he had resented ever since the beheading of John the Baptist that Jesus had not saved John. Every time his hopes soared and Jesus dashed them, a scar of bitter resentment was left behind. The other apostles had also craved worldly honor in their minds, but with their hearts they loved Jesus.
ch44.b025: That evening, since it was Wednesday, the camp held its social hour, and Judas was back, intoxicated with thoughts of grandeur. The Master tried to cheer his downcast apostles, but it was nearly impossible. He asked carefully about each of their families and, looking at David Zebedee, asked whether anyone had heard lately from his mother or his family. David looked down at his feet.
ch44.b026: Jesus warned them not to trust the support of the multitude, who believed with their minds but had not let the truth strike living roots into their hearts. “⟦Q 177:5.2⟧Some who have been very close to us have already made up their minds to desert. You have rested today in preparation for those times which are now upon us. Watch, therefore, and pray that on the morrow you may be strengthened for the days that are just ahead.⟦/Q⟧” Silent messengers came and went, speaking only to David. Before the evening was over, some knew that Lazarus had fled in haste from Bethany. John Mark was ominously silent. Even the Master’s good cheer frightened them. This Wednesday evening was the low-tide mark of their spirits until the hour of his death.
ch44.b027: Just before midnight Jesus, knowing that this was the last night he would ever sleep through with his chosen family on earth, sent them off to rest. “⟦Q 177:5.6⟧Go to your sleep, my brethren, and peace be upon you till we rise on the morrow, one more day to do the Father’s will and experience the joy of knowing that we are his sons.⟦/Q⟧”
ch45.title: The Last Supper
ch45.b002: Thursday was the last free day Jesus would spend on earth as a divine Son incarnated in the flesh. Soon after breakfast on that beautiful morning he led the apostles and about fifty trusted disciples to a secluded spot a short distance above the camp, and for almost two hours he taught them and answered their questions about the relation of the kingdom of heaven to the kingdoms of this world. Judas was not there. Peter and several others remarked on his absence; some supposed the Master had sent him into the city to arrange the details of the Passover.
ch45.b003: There was nothing incompatible, Jesus taught, between sonship in the spiritual kingdom and citizenship in an earthly government. It was the believer’s duty to render to Caesar the things that were Caesar’s and to God the things that were God’s. They must never render spiritual worship to earthly rulers, nor use the power of governments to further the spiritual kingdom. Having become sons of the kingdom, they should be all the better citizens. “⟦Q 178:1.7⟧Be you always as wise as serpents but as harmless as doves.⟦/Q⟧” They might always labor to persuade men’s minds, but they must never dare to compel them, and they must not forget the great law of fairness: “⟦Q 178:1.12⟧Whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do even so to them.⟦/Q⟧”
ch45.b004: The gospel, he said, was like the seed of a living being, which from generation to generation unfolds itself in new forms to meet the needs of each new age. “⟦Q 178:1.15⟧It must not be permitted to become merely a sacred memory, a mere tradition about me and the times in which we now live.⟦/Q⟧” And he ended: “⟦Q 178:1.17⟧Throughout the vicissitudes of life, remember always to love one another. Do not strive with men, even with unbelievers.⟦/Q⟧” Few of his hearers took in even part of it. The Greeks understood the most. Even the eleven were bewildered that he should speak of long ages of gospel work to come when his own ministry seemed so near its end.
ch45.b005: The Man with the Water Pitcher
ch45.b006: By noon everyone in the camp had heard of Lazarus’s hasty flight from Bethany. David Zebedee, through his secret agents in Jerusalem, knew all about the plan to arrest and kill Jesus and about the part Judas was playing in it, though he told no one. Shortly after lunch he led Jesus aside and began to ask whether he knew. The Master held up his hand and stopped him. “⟦Q 178:2.3⟧Yes, David, I know all about it, and I know that you know, but see to it that you tell no man. Only doubt not in your own heart that the will of God will prevail in the end.⟦/Q⟧” Just then a runner arrived from Philadelphia: Abner had heard of the plot and asked whether he should come to Jerusalem. Jesus sent back this word: “⟦Q 178:2.4⟧Go on with your work. If I depart from you in the flesh, it is only that I may return in the spirit. I will not forsake you. I will be with you to the end.⟦/Q⟧”
ch45.b007: About that time Philip asked where they should prepare to eat the Passover. Jesus told him to bring Peter and John. When Judas drew closer to overhear, David Zebedee stepped up and engaged him in conversation. Then Jesus said to the three: “⟦Q 178:2.7⟧Go immediately into Jerusalem, and as you enter the gate, you will meet a man bearing a water pitcher. He will speak to you, and then shall you follow him.⟦/Q⟧” They were to ask the master of the house where the guest chamber was, and he would show them a large upper room, furnished and ready. Near the gate they met the man with the pitcher and followed him to the home of John Mark, whose father showed them the upper room. All this had been arranged between the Master and John Mark the day before in the hills, so that Judas would not learn of the meeting place in advance.
ch45.b008: Meanwhile Judas handed David some money for provisions. David asked whether, under the circumstances, it might be well to give him a little in advance. Judas thought a moment and said it would be best to turn over all the money to him, since they were plotting against the Master and, if anything happened to Judas, David would not be hampered. So David received all the apostolic funds. The others did not learn of it until the next evening.
ch45.b010: About half past four the three returned to say that all was ready, and Jesus set out with the twelve for Jerusalem. It was the last journey he ever made with all twelve of them. Avoiding the crowds in the Kidron valley, they crossed the western brow of Olivet to the Bethany road, and when they came near the place where he had spoken the evening before about the destruction of Jerusalem, they stopped without thinking and looked down in silence on the city. Since they were early and he did not wish to pass through the city until after sunset, he had them sit down. “⟦Q 178:3.2⟧As the Father sent me into this world, so am I about to send you forth to represent me and finish the work I have begun.⟦/Q⟧” They must not needlessly expose themselves to peril when men came to take the Son of Man. “⟦Q 178:3.3⟧I need no defense by the hand of man; the armies of heaven are even now near at hand; but I am determined to do the will of my Father in heaven.⟦/Q⟧” In his Father’s universe were many abodes, and when they had finished their work on earth, they too would come to his joy.
ch45.b011: Then he rose, and they followed him down Olivet and into the city. Night was falling over the narrow streets. The crowds jostled them, but no one recognized them, nor knew that the Son of God was passing by on his way to his last mortal meeting with his chosen ambassadors. Except for three, the apostles did not know where they were going. Neither did they know that one of their own number had already conspired to betray the Master. John Mark had followed them to the gate, and then ran ahead by another street so that he was waiting to welcome them at his father’s house.
ch45.b013: After greeting John Mark’s father and mother, the apostles went straight up to the upper chamber while Jesus stayed behind to talk with the family. It was a large room, completely furnished for the supper. Bread, wine, water, and herbs stood ready at one end of a long U-shaped table, and around the rest of the table were thirteen reclining couches, such as a well-to-do Jewish household would provide for the Passover. Just inside the door stood pitchers of water, basins, and towels for washing their dusty feet. It had been understood that the Master would celebrate this occasion alone with the twelve, so no servant had been provided. The apostles began to look at one another. Each thought within himself, Who shall wash our feet? And each thought that it would not be he.
ch45.b014: As they hesitated, Judas stepped over to the seat of honor at the left of the host and made it plain that he meant to recline there. At once John Zebedee claimed the next preferred seat, on the host’s right. Simon Peter was so enraged that, as the others looked on, he marched clear around the table and took the lowest couch, at the very end. He did it partly in protest, and partly in the hope that Jesus, finding him in the place of least honor, would call him up higher and displace one who had presumed to honor himself. The rest found places until all were seated: on the right of the Master, John; on the left, Judas, then Simon Zelotes, Matthew, James Zebedee, Andrew, the Alpheus twins, Philip, Nathaniel, Thomas, and Simon Peter.
ch45.b015: They were still voicing angry recriminations when the Master appeared in the doorway. He hesitated a moment, and a look of disappointment slowly crept over his face. Without comment he went to his place, and he did not disturb their seating. Their feet were still unwashed.
ch45.b017: For a few moments no one spoke. Jesus looked them all over and, relieving the tension with a smile, said: “⟦Q 179:2.1⟧I have greatly desired to eat this Passover with you. I wanted to eat with you once more before I suffered, and realizing that my hour has come, I arranged to have this supper with you tonight.⟦/Q⟧” When the wine and water had been mixed, he took the cup from the hand of Thaddeus and offered thanks. “⟦Q 179:2.2⟧Take this cup and divide it among yourselves and, when you partake of it, realize that I shall not again drink with you the fruit of the vine since this is our last supper. When we sit down again in this manner, it will be in the kingdom to come.⟦/Q⟧”
ch45.b018: After the first cup Jesus rose from the table and went silently to the door where the pitchers and basins stood. They watched in growing astonishment as he took off his outer garment, girded himself with a towel, and poured water into a basin. Then he made his way around the empty end of the table to the lowest seat, where Simon Peter reclined, and knelt down in the attitude of a servant. All twelve rose to their feet as one man; even Judas forgot himself for a moment and stood with the rest.
ch45.b019: There stood Peter, looking down into the upturned face of his Master. Jesus said nothing. At last Peter spoke for them all: “⟦Q 179:3.3⟧Master, do you really mean to wash my feet?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus answered, “⟦Q 179:3.3⟧You may not fully understand what I am about to do, but hereafter you will know the meaning of all these things.⟦/Q⟧” Peter drew a long breath. “⟦Q 179:3.3⟧Master, you shall never wash my feet!⟦/Q⟧” Each of the others nodded his approval.
ch45.b020: “⟦Q 179:3.5⟧Peter, I declare that, if I do not wash your feet, you will have no part with me in that which I am about to perform.⟦/Q⟧” Then, in his impetuous way, Peter cried, “⟦Q 179:3.5⟧Then, Master, wash not my feet only but also my hands and my head.⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said: “⟦Q 179:3.6⟧He who is already clean needs only to have his feet washed. You who sit with me tonight are clean—but not all.⟦/Q⟧” In silence he went around the table and washed the feet of all twelve, not even passing by Judas. The scene touched even Judas at first, but when his vainglorious intellect judged it, he concluded that this gesture of humility was one more proof that Jesus would never be Israel’s deliverer.
ch45.b021: Jesus put on his cloak, returned to his place, and looked at his bewildered apostles. “⟦Q 179:3.8⟧Do you really understand what I have done to you? You call me Master, and you say well, for so I am. If, then, the Master has washed your feet, why was it that you were unwilling to wash one another’s feet? … Verily, verily, I say to you: A servant is not greater than his master; neither is one who is sent greater than he who sends him.⟦/Q⟧” Did they not know that there could be no place of preferment at his table, that he loved each of them as he did the others? “⟦Q 179:3.9⟧Who is the greater, he who sits at meat, or he who serves? Is it not commonly regarded that he who sits at meat is the greater? But you will observe that I am among you as one who serves.⟦/Q⟧”
ch45.b023: The Alpheus twins brought on the bread and wine, the bitter herbs, and the paste of dried fruits. For some minutes the apostles ate in silence, but the Master’s cheerfulness soon drew them into conversation. About the middle of the second course, Jesus told them that he would not be with them by this time tomorrow night. “⟦Q 179:4.1⟧Now has my hour come, but it was not required that one of you should betray me into the hands of my enemies.⟦/Q⟧”
ch45.b024: They looked at one another and asked hesitantly, “Is it I?” Jesus said that while it was necessary that he go to the Father, it was not required that one of them become a traitor. “⟦Q 179:4.2⟧My friend of many years, who even now eats my bread, will be willing to betray me, even as he now dips his hand with me in the dish.⟦/Q⟧” Again they asked, “Is it I?” And when Judas, on his left, asked, “Is it I?” Jesus dipped the bread in the dish of herbs, handed it to him, and said, “You have said.” The others did not hear. John leaned over and asked who it was, and Jesus answered, “⟦Q 179:4.3⟧Already have I told you, even he to whom I gave the sop.⟦/Q⟧” But it was so natural for the host to give the sop to the guest on his left that no one took notice. Peter, highly excited, leaned across the table and urged John to ask the Master who it was.
ch45.b025: Jesus ended their whispering. He told them these things, he said, so that afterward they would remember that he had known and had forewarned them, and might be strengthened for the trials ahead. Then he leaned toward Judas: “⟦Q 179:4.6⟧What you have decided to do, do quickly.⟦/Q⟧” Judas rose and hastily left the room, going out into the night. The others supposed he had gone to buy something more for the supper or to run some errand, since they thought he still carried the bag. The Master had started with twelve; now he had eleven. This supper, with its tender episodes and softening touches, had been his last appeal to Judas, but it was of no avail when love was once really dead.
ch45.b027: When they brought him the third cup, the “cup of blessing,” Jesus rose, took it in his hands, and blessed it. “⟦Q 179:5.1⟧Take this cup, all of you, and drink of it. This shall be the cup of my remembrance. This is the cup of the blessing of a new dispensation of grace and truth. This shall be to you the emblem of the bestowal and ministry of the divine Spirit of Truth. And I will not again drink this cup with you until I drink in new form with you in the Father’s eternal kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” The apostles drank in profound reverence and perfect silence, sensing that something out of the ordinary was taking place.
ch45.b028: Then he took the bread and, after giving thanks, broke it and passed it around. “⟦Q 179:5.3⟧Take this bread of remembrance and eat it. I have told you that I am the bread of life. And this bread of life is the united life of the Father and the Son in one gift. The word of the Father, as revealed in the Son, is indeed the bread of life.⟦/Q⟧” The old Passover had commemorated their fathers’ emergence from slavery; the new remembrance supper was the symbol of a new dispensation, in which the individual emerges from the bondage of ceremonialism and selfishness into the joyous fellowship of the liberated faith sons of God. As always, the Master spoke in symbols. He did not wish to establish a precise form or to bind his meanings in the dead chains of tradition and dogma, but to set man’s reborn soul free.
ch45.b029: When he had thus established the supper of remembrance, he said to the eleven: “⟦Q 179:5.9⟧And as often as you do this, do it in remembrance of me. And when you do remember me, first look back upon my life in the flesh, recall that I was once with you, and then, by faith, discern that you shall all sometime sup with me in the Father’s eternal kingdom. This is the new Passover which I leave with you.⟦/Q⟧” There was nothing of sacred form or ceremonial consecration about the supper or the room; it took place in the upper chamber of a friend, without ecclesiastical sanction. And they ended that celebration of the old but bloodless Passover by singing, all together, the one hundred and eighteenth Psalm.
ch46.title: The Farewell Discourse
ch46.b002: The last notes of the Psalm died away in the upper chamber, and the apostles supposed that the Master would now go straight back to the camp. Instead he motioned them to sit down. In the flickering lamplight the eleven settled again on their couches around the table.
ch46.b003: He began by reminding them of other days. “⟦Q 180:0.2⟧You well remember when I sent you forth without purse or wallet and even advised that you take with you no extra clothes. And you will all recall that you lacked nothing. But now have you come upon troublous times. No longer can you depend upon the good will of the multitudes. Henceforth, he who has a purse, let him take it with him.⟦/Q⟧” When they went out to proclaim the gospel, they must make such provision for their support as seemed best. “⟦Q 180:0.2⟧I have come to bring peace, but it will not appear for a time.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b004: Then he said: “⟦Q 180:0.3⟧The time has now come for the Son of Man to be glorified, and the Father shall be glorified in me. My friends, I am to be with you only a little longer. Soon you will seek for me, but you will not find me, for I am going to a place to which you cannot, at this time, come.⟦/Q⟧” But when they had finished their work on earth, as he had now finished his, they would come to him. They would see him no more on earth, but they would all see him in the age to come, when they ascended to the kingdom his Father had given him.
ch46.b006: After a few moments of informal conversation, Jesus stood up. When he had enacted the parable of the basin and towel, he had promised them a new commandment, and now, as he was about to leave them, he would give it. They knew the commandment to love their neighbor as themselves, but he was not wholly satisfied even with that sincere devotion. “⟦Q 180:1.1⟧And so I give you this new commandment: That you love one another even as I have loved you. And by this will all men know that you are my disciples if you thus love one another.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b007: This commandment, he said, was no new burden but a new joy, the delight of bestowing the heart’s affection upon one’s fellows. “⟦Q 180:1.3⟧Greater love can no man have than this: that he will lay down his life for his friends. And you are my friends; you will continue to be my friends if you are but willing to do what I have taught you. You have called me Master, but I do not call you servants.⟦/Q⟧” They had not merely chosen him; he had also chosen them, and ordained them to go into the world and yield the fruit of loving service to their fellows, even as he had lived among them and revealed the Father.
ch46.b008: It was loyalty, not sacrifice, that he asked of them. The service of a friend for a friend can never be called a sacrifice. At the beginning he had taught them that they were sons of God, and he had called them brethren. Now, before he left them, he called them his friends.
ch46.b010: Then Jesus stood up again and went on teaching:

ch46.b011.en: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. I am the vine, and you are the branches. And the Father requires of me only that you shall bear much fruit. The vine is pruned only to increase the fruitfulness of its branches. … You must abide in me, and I in you; the branch will die if it is separated from the vine. As the branch cannot bear fruit except it abides in the vine, so neither can you yield the fruits of loving service except you abide in me. …

ch46.b013.en: “As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Live in my love even as I live in the Father’s love.”

ch46.b014: As he spoke, the apostles remembered the great emblem of the grape and its vine that adorned the entrance to Herod’s temple. The Jews had long taught that the Messiah would be “⟦Q 180:2.3⟧a stem arising out of the vine⟦/Q⟧” of David’s ancestors.
ch46.b015: That night Jesus also spoke of prayer: if they abode in him and his words lived in them, they might ask whatever his spirit willed, with the assurance that the Father would grant it. Great sorrow later came from misunderstanding these words. Believers came to regard prayer in Jesus’ name as a sort of supreme magic, and for centuries honest souls wrecked their faith against that stumbling block. Prayer is not a process of getting your own way but a program of taking God’s way, of learning to recognize and do the Father’s will. When the branch of the vine is alive, there can be only one answer to all its petitions: increased grape bearing.
ch46.b017: The eleven had scarcely finished talking over the vine and the branches when the Master, knowing his time was short, spoke again. “⟦Q 180:3.1⟧If the world shall hate you, you should recall that it hated me even before it hated you.⟦/Q⟧” They were in the world, but their lives were not to be worldlike. “⟦Q 180:3.1⟧The servant is not greater than his master. If they dare to persecute me, they will also persecute you.⟦/Q⟧” And what had he done to these men that they should hate him so terribly? “⟦Q 180:3.2⟧Nothing, save to offer them fellowship on earth and salvation in heaven. But have you not read in the Scripture the saying: ‘And they hated me without a cause’?⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b018: Yet he would not leave them alone in the world. “⟦Q 180:3.4⟧Let not your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; continue to believe also in me.⟦/Q⟧” In his Father’s universe there were many tarrying-places, and he was going back to those worlds of light; and if he went before them, he would surely send for them, that they might be with him.
ch46.b019: When Jesus sat down, Thomas rose: they did not know where he was going, so of course they did not know the way, but they would follow him that very night if he would show them. Jesus answered: “⟦Q 180:3.7⟧Thomas, I am the way, the truth, and the life. No man goes to the Father except through me. All who find the Father, first find me. If you know me, you know the way to the Father.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b020: This was too deep for Philip. After a few words with Nathaniel, he stood up. “⟦Q 180:3.8⟧Master, show us the Father, and everything you have said will be made plain.⟦/Q⟧” Jesus said: “⟦Q 180:3.9⟧Philip, have I been so long with you and yet you do not even now know me? Again do I declare: He who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you then say, Show us the Father?⟦/Q⟧” As the Master went aside to refresh himself with water, the eleven fell into a spirited discussion, and Peter was just beginning an extended speech when Jesus returned and beckoned them to be seated.
ch46.b022: He promised them a new helper. When he had gone to the Father and received the final sovereignty of his domain, he would ask the Father to let him pour out the Spirit of Truth upon all flesh. “⟦Q 180:4.1⟧I will not leave you desolate. Today I can be with you only in person. In the times to come I will be with you and all other men who desire my presence, wherever you may be, and with each of you at the same time. Do you not discern that it is better for me to go away; that I leave you in the flesh so that I may the better and the more fully be with you in the spirit?⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b023: As he paused, Judas Alpheus ventured one of the few questions he or his brother ever asked Jesus in public: the Master had always lived among them as a friend; how would they know him when he showed himself only by this spirit? Jesus looked down upon them all and smiled. “⟦Q 180:4.5⟧My little children, I am going away, going back to my Father. In a little while you will not see me as you do here, as flesh and blood. In a very short time I am going to send you my spirit, just like me except for this material body.⟦/Q⟧” This new teacher would live in each of their hearts, and so all the children of light would be made one. Judas Alpheus did not fully understand, but he grasped the promise of the new teacher, and from the look on Andrew’s face he knew his question had been well answered.
ch46.b024: The new helper would not be the letter or law of truth, but the conviction of truth, the spirit of living and growing truth. Truth can be known and lived, but it cannot be imprisoned in formulas, codes, or creeds; when men try to do so, it speedily dies. Even the golden rule, taken only literally and without the insight of the Spirit of Truth, may wound one’s fellows. Spirit-led believers understand it as a call so to relate themselves to others that they receive the highest possible good from the contact. The old religion taught self-sacrifice; the new gospel teaches self-forgetfulness and true self-realization in loving service.
ch46.b026: He warned them again that the hour was coming when those who killed them would think they were doing God a service. Then he said he was surprised that none of them had asked, Why do you leave us? “⟦Q 180:6.2,180:6.3⟧It is really profitable for you that I go away. If I go not away, the new teacher cannot come into your hearts. … I have yet much to say to you, but you cannot stand any more just now. Albeit, when he, the Spirit of Truth, comes, he shall eventually guide you into all truth.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b027: “⟦Q 180:6.5⟧In just a little while I will leave you for a short time.⟦/Q⟧” The apostles whispered among themselves. What did he mean by this “little while” and “not for long”? Jesus knew their question. He had plainly told them, he said, that the Son of Man must die but would rise again. “⟦Q 180:6.7⟧A woman is indeed sorrowful in the hour of her travail, but when she is once delivered of her child, she immediately forgets her anguish in the joy of the knowledge that a man has been born into the world. And so are you about to sorrow over my departure, but I will soon see you again, and then will your sorrow be turned into rejoicing.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b028: The eleven said to one another, “⟦Q 180:6.9⟧Behold, he does speak plainly to us. Surely the Master did come forth from God. But why does he say he must return to the Father?⟦/Q⟧” Jesus saw that they still did not understand. They could not get away from their long-cherished ideas of the Messiah.
ch46.b030: After the discourse they talked together of many things, and slowly it began to dawn on them that their friend and teacher was really going to leave them. Then Jesus called them to order once more. “⟦Q 181:1.5⟧Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I make these gifts not as the world gives—by measure—I give each of you all you will receive. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.⟦/Q⟧” When they were scattered, every man to his own place, leaving him in the hands of his enemies, he would not be alone; the Father was always with him. “⟦Q 181:1.6⟧In this world you will have tribulation, but be of good cheer; I have triumphed in the world and shown you the way to eternal joy and everlasting service.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b031: It was neither the peace of the stoic, resolved to endure the worst, nor the hope of the optimist, longing for a peace that never comes. It was the peace of a son who fully believes that his career for time and eternity is safely in the keeping of an all-wise and all-loving Father.
ch46.b033: Then the Master went around the table to say good-bye to each man in turn, and each rose to his feet when Jesus spoke to him. To John he entrusted the care of his earthly family. “⟦Q 181:2.4⟧You should become the apostle of the new commandment which I have this night given you. Dedicate your life to teaching your brethren how to love one another, even as I have loved you.⟦/Q⟧” With tears rolling down his cheeks, John asked how he could learn to love his brethren more. “⟦Q 181:2.5⟧You will learn to love your brethren more when you first learn to love their Father in heaven more.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b034: Passing around his own seat, Jesus paused a moment beside the empty place of Judas Iscariot, and his face was sad. The apostles wondered at it, but none of them, except possibly Andrew, had the slightest thought that their treasurer had gone out to betray his Master.
ch46.b035: To Simon Zelotes he said, “⟦Q 181:2.7⟧You are a true son of Abraham, but what a time I have had trying to make you a son of this heavenly kingdom.⟦/Q⟧” Simon, drying his eyes, protested that he would never falter. Jesus laid a hand on his shoulder. He did not doubt that Simon would go forth in battle and die for him, but that would not be required. None of the apostles would be so upset and disheartened after his departure, yet through all that season of discouragement his spirit would abide with Simon. To Matthew he said, “⟦Q 181:2.14⟧Dedicate your whole future life service to showing all men that God is no respecter of persons.⟦/Q⟧” To James he spoke of drinking his cup and urged him to possess his soul in patience and to learn “⟦Q 181:2.15⟧that true wisdom embraces discretion as well as courage.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b036: He released Andrew from all administrative responsibility, but charged him to hold his brethren together with a firm and loving hand through the trying days ahead. To the Alpheus twins he said that they might return to their former labors gladly, knowing that “⟦Q 181:2.19⟧to him who is God-knowing, there is no such thing as common labor or secular toil.⟦/Q⟧” To Philip he said, “⟦Q 181:2.20⟧And always remember, Philip, he who has seen me has seen the Father.⟦/Q⟧” He bade Nathaniel be seated, sat down beside him, and told him that “⟦Q 181:2.21⟧sincerity is most serviceable in the work of the kingdom when it is wedded to discretion.⟦/Q⟧” And to Thomas he said: “⟦Q 181:2.26⟧Your doubts have perplexed your brethren, but they have never troubled me. I have confidence in you, and I will go before you even to the uttermost parts of the earth.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b037: Last of all he came to Simon Peter. He was distressed, he said, that Peter had not yet learned to think before he spoke, and he warned them all: “⟦Q 181:2.27⟧This night you will all be in great danger of stumbling over me. You know it is written, ‘The shepherd will be smitten and the sheep will be scattered abroad.’⟦/Q⟧” Peter put his hand on Jesus’ shoulder. “⟦Q 181:2.28⟧No matter if all my brethren should succumb to doubts because of you, I promise that I will not stumble over anything you may do. I will go with you and, if need be, die for you.⟦/Q⟧” Peter stood there trembling with emotion and overflowing with genuine love, and Jesus looked straight into his moistened eyes. “⟦Q 181:2.29⟧Peter, verily, verily, I say to you, this night the cock will not crow until you have denied me three or four times.⟦/Q⟧”
ch46.b038: Then he spoke to all of them. “⟦Q 181:2.30⟧I love you all with the love wherewith the Father loves me, and therefore should you henceforth love one another, even as I have loved you.⟦/Q⟧” And when they had sung a hymn, they departed for the camp on the Mount of Olives.
